transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-10-07
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: 60 minutes
Location: All-hands (virtual)
Attendees: Samir, Emily, Noah, Priya, Liam, Janelle + company-wide

[00:00] Samir Patel: Hey everyone, welcome to the October all-hands, uh, thanks for joining. We've got a packed agenda — Q3 recap, product, reliability, hiring and then Q&A. I'm gonna kick us off with numbers.

[00:28] Samir Patel: So Q3 — overall revenue growth was in line with plan, ARR up low-double digits versus Q2. Net dollar retention continues to be strong with a couple of expansion deals, we won a big dedicated contract in EMEA, shout out to the sales team. There are some notes on churn — we had a few pilot churns where latency expectations weren't met. We'll talk about that in product.

[00:56] Emily Ramos: Quick add — usage on Redwood API grew 35% month-over-month for our top 50 customers, embeddings volume increased thanks to the semantic search IR bundles, um, and our latency p95 for hosted endpoints improved after the September kernel tuning. Not perfect everywhere, but trending the right way.

[01:20] Noah Kim: On reliability — we had the Sept 18th incident; root cause was a KV cache invalidation bug combined with a missed autoscaling signal. We reverted the change quickly, but we need stronger guardrails around cache promo, promoh — promoter, sorry, around cache invalidations. We're introducing an automated canary for cache churn and stricter rollout windows.

[01:52] Priya Singh: Engineering is prioritizing three reliability items: better observability for prefix cache hits, auto-throttling fallback for busy nodes, and additional end-to-end tests for model variant routing. The dynamic batching changes we've been piloting should reduce tail latency, fingers crossed, and we'll share benchmarks next week.

[02:22] Liam O'Connor: From sales — momentum in financial services and vertical SaaS. Two headline deals: Enterprise corp in EMEA committed to Dedicated; and a PLG-to-sales motion customer upgraded to reserved capacity. The playbook for Dedicated is working, but pricing feedback: customers sometimes prefer host-hosted vs dedicated because of cost predictability. We need clearer comms on burst capacity and pricing.

[02:50] Janelle Wu: People update — hiring sprint continues, we closed a few IC roles in infra, and we've opened senior infra manager and head of developer experience. Interview slates are filling up; please join panels when asked. Also rolling out new parental leave policy next month.

[03:10] Samir Patel: Roadmap highlight — three things: 1) Redwood API improvements (streaming and function calling enhancements), 2) Redwood Dedicated scaling and autoscaling policy UI, 3) Redwood Private — VPC/on-prem pathing, plus KMS integrations. We want the same developer experience everywhere.

[03:40] Emily Ramos: Product deep-dive — API v2 will include structured output templates and better tool-calling semantics. We also have an optimization feature (Optimize) that suggests batching and quant profiles per workload; it's in closed beta with a few customers. For Dedicated, we've been tuning kernel selection and adding an auto-quantization path for some models which reduces cost on common seq lengths.

[04:05] (crosstalk) Unknown: "auto-quant..."

[04:10] Noah Kim: Quick note on Private — customers ask for audit logs and HSM/KMS support; both teams are working on integrations. We plan to release KMS support for our on-prem package by end of Q4. There are some infra constraints but we have implementation partners lined up.

[04:36] Samir Patel: Ok let's cover incidents and what we learned. Noah — can you take us through the postmortem?

[04:42] Noah Kim: Yep. On Sept 18, a config change unintentionally flipped a cache TTL to zero for a shard group. That caused a cascade as nodes tried to re-populate KV entries and hit a throttling limit on the underlying storage tier. Autoscaling didn't trigger because the metric we relied on was smoothed; we changed the metric window to be more sensitive to rapid cache churn. Lessons: tighter changelists, more aggressive canaries, and a manual rollback runbook.

[05:14] Emily Ramos: We're also going to add customer-facing incident pages with more proactive alerts for SRE and customers who opt in; basically easier status and postmortem links.

[05:28] Samir Patel: Thanks. Now, product wins — quick shoutouts. Priya, engineering, great job on the batching throughput work. Liam, sales, great work on the EMEA Dedicated deal.

[05:40] Priya Singh: Thanks — just to be clear, the batching improvements are shipping in staged rollouts; you might see slight perf regressions in some edge cases during ramp, we'll monitor closely.

[05:56] (15 sec silence)

[06:12] Samir Patel: Moving on to finances — CFO couldn't make it today so quick updates: burn is slightly better than plan; runway extended by a couple of months based on renewal cadence. We remain focused on efficiency.

[06:28] Samir Patel: Now open floor Q&A — please raise hands in chat, we'll take pre-submitted Qs first.

[06:40] Q: "What is priority between Dedicated vs Private for next quarter?" (from chat)

[06:46] Emily Ramos: Short answer: both. Dedicated gets engineering scale investments because it's where we see predictable committed revenue and higher ARPU, Private is strategic for regulated customers. We'll sequence work to enable both — Dedicated autoscaling and Private KMS are top two.

[07:10] Q: "Any updates on model catalog — will we host newer open models?"

[07:16] Noah Kim: Yes, model onboarding is ongoing. We're adding a few Llama-family variants and some tuned instruction models; the challenge is optimizing kernels and quant profiles. We'll publish a compatibility matrix soon.

[07:36] Q: "How do we measure success for Optimize?"

[07:40] Emily Ramos: Measure by token cost reduction and latency impact per workload; we also look at customer adoption and quality regressions. Optimize will have a quality guardrail where we flag prompts with potential regressions and require human approval to apply aggressive quantization.

[08:00] Samir Patel: Quick comment on competition — we watch OpenAI, Anthropic, HF, Bedrock. Our angle is predictable unit economics and ops controls.

[08:20] Liam O'Connor: Sales ask — Product folks, can we create a concise one-pager on Dedicated pricing and burst options? Customers frequently ask about burst capacity and fallback to hosted.

[08:30] Emily Ramos: Yes, we'll produce a playbook and an FAQ for sales. Emily to coordinate with Liam. (laughs) that's me.

[08:40] Janelle Wu: HR question from the chat — "Any update on manager training and compensation calibration?"

[08:46] Janelle Wu: We're running calibration sessions next week; managers should expect invites. Compensation reviews will be synced to the leveling doc.

[09:08] Engineer: "Are we planning more observability signals for private installs?"

[09:12] Noah Kim: Yes, Private will include optional tracing hooks and audit logs. We need to balance telemetry with customer privacy concerns. We'll offer a signed template for allowed telemetry fields.

[09:30] Product PM: "Timeline for API v2 release?"

[09:34] Emily Ramos: We aim for beta in late November, GA early Q1. Beta will include structured outputs and function calling improvements.

[09:48] (crosstalk) Someone: "Will that include stable streaming?"

[09:52] Emily Ramos: Yes, streaming improvements are part of v2. Also better backpressure handling.

[10:02] Samir Patel: Ok, quick org note — we are reorganizing the infra teams into two clear squads: serving runtime and orchestration. Priya will lead serving runtime, and a new role will lead orchestration. This should reduce handoffs and speed up rollouts.

[10:28] Priya Singh: We'll publish the new org chart and clear RACI for cross-team features.

[10:40] Samir Patel: Final remarks — focus on reliability and delivering on the Dedicated commitments. Please take the action items seriously. And thanks to everyone for the hard work this quarter.

[10:56] Samir Patel: We'll do a shorter leadership sync next week for execs only. All-hands again next month.

[11:05] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcript quality: automated transcript with occasional mis-attributions and misspellings (e.g., "cache promo" instead of cache 'promote', "auto-quant" truncated at times). Some timestamps approximate.
